recurring_harms: discrimination against historically underserved groups;delayed or denied access to essential services;over-trusted automation masking real errors
human_in_loop_decisions: Any decision that downgrades urgency, denies or delays access, or rejects a person needs an immediate, empowered human review and override before the person is told the negative outcome
strongest_guardrails: Mandatory subgroup/bias evaluation before each release;a hard block on any fully-automated negative outcome without human sign-off;independent external validation against the actual deployment population before go-live
cross_industry_pattern: Across hiring and healthcare-assistant products, the dominant harm driver is not model sophistication but historical proxy data, such as cost or utilization in health and prior outcomes in hiring, that silently encodes whose needs were undercounted in the past; both sectors need mandatory subgroup evaluation and a hard human-override release gate written into the launch checklist, not just a general governance framework like NIST's Govern-Map-Measure-Manage, before any release.
